boundaries.budget: VM step, requested-live-payload and call-depth limits stop evaluation with a stopped resource ledger; they are not semantic traps, allocator failure results or source cancellation. Native code does not inherit evaluator quotas.
boundaries.cancel: Composite tasks and the owned-state queue implement explicit cooperative transitions. A VM budget stop, process signal, or host interruption is not a general source cancellation/unwind operation.
boundaries.concurrent: Core excludes arbitrary threads, shared mutable memory, atomics and MMIO. Host dispatcher locks and safe-point checks do not establish a general concurrent-language memory model.
boundaries.crash: An incomplete or forcibly terminated native observation is rejected. The host retains process-cleanup ownership until termination/reap is confirmed, and a later reap cannot turn the failed observation into a successful return. Guest cleanup, guest resource ledgers, persistent-state recovery and replay safety are not established.
boundaries.error: Errors represented as values use the same checked normal-return rules. A failed fallible allocation still produces a logical empty owner that must be consumed.
boundaries.normal: Local owned resources and loans must be consumed or transferred through a checked signature; explicit v8 returned loans retain parameter origins and suspend callers until children end.
boundaries.recursive: Core recursive calls and finite owned chains are separate from static finite-budget profiles. Native recursion/stack bounds and universal termination are not established.
boundaries.trap: The VM reports the stopped resource ledger. Native traps abort. No destructor recovery, exception unwinding, or cleanup completion theorem is claimed.
